messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

our working plan for the North Quad Film Society's October program is to hold three Thursday screenings, on October 8, October 15, and October 22, 2026. The first film is City in Rain, with a running time of 84 minutes; the second is a group of shorts called Paper Moons, with a combined running time of 47 minutes; and the third is Last Stop, which runs for 91 minutes. We are asking the campus events office to reserve room B214 for each date. The room has 92 seats, and the film society would like to keep 12 of them available for students who arrive without registering. Doors are planned to open at 6:15 p.m., with each screening starting at 6:45 p.m. The start time should stay the same on all three dates, so students do not have to interpret a different schedule every week.

The draft schedule leaves room for a brief welcome before each screening, but it does not include a discussion afterward. For City in Rain, the film's distributor has quoted a runtime of 84 minutes, while the copy in the society's archive lists 83 minutes. The program coordinator is asking the distributor to verify which runtime should go on the public listing; until they reply, the 84-minute figure is the one in this draft. Paper Moons is made up of four shorts, and the 47-minute figure is the combined runtime supplied by the filmmaker. Last Stop has a 91-minute runtime on its licensing sheet. These times do not include introductions, and the society has not promised that every screening will finish at a particular time. The draft assumes that the welcome will take no more than five minutes, but it remains a planning estimate.

Room B214 is on the second floor of North Quad Hall. The building entrance on Cedar Walk has a ramp, and the events office directory lists an elevator near the east stairwell. We are asking the office to confirm that the elevator will be operating on all three evenings and that the room's aisle layout can accommodate a wheelchair user without blocking an exit. The society's access lead, Mina Patel, has also asked whether the room can be unlocked 30 minutes before doors open, so volunteers have time to check the projector and place the printed program sheets. If the room cannot be opened by 5:45 p.m., the access lead wants the society to move the equipment check to the student lounge rather than shorten the planned check. That is a request for the events office to consider, not a confirmed alternative booking.

The volunteer plan is organized around four roles, with the same assignments expected to apply on each date unless a volunteer reports a conflict.
1. The program coordinator will introduce the film and give the welcome. The coordinator is also responsible for checking that the announced running time matches the public listing once the distributor confirms the figure for City in Rain.
2. Two door volunteers will check student IDs and count attendance. They should record the number of people entering, not the number of seats left, and they should keep the 12 walk-in seats visible on the seating chart until the screening begins. The society has not decided whether any unused reserved seats will be released early.
3. One projection volunteer will test the playback file and sound level before doors open. For Paper Moons, that person should check all four shorts in their listed order and confirm that the combined file does not begin with the filmmaker's slate. The filmmaker has said, "the slate is for review, not for the audience," and the society is asking whether a version without the slate can be provided.
4. One access volunteer will keep the ramp-side aisle clear and bring the large-print program sheets to the entrance. The society has printed 18 large-print copies, based on requests received so far, but that number is not a cap on requests at the door.

The room request should be tracked under the filename below, because the campus events office asked the society to use one filename for the attendance estimate and equipment notes. The file is a working document, not a confirmed room reservation. The current estimate is 74 attendees on October 8, 68 on October 15, and 80 on October 22. Each number is an estimate for that date, not a count of registrations. The equipment notes ask for one HDMI cable, two handheld microphones, and a standing lamp at the entrance. The projection volunteer has already checked that the society owns one HDMI adapter, but has not checked whether it works with the room's projector.

delivery-summary.tsv

For publicity, the society is preparing one digital poster and 60 printed copies for the student center and the library noticeboard. The poster draft includes all three dates, the 6:45 p.m. start time, and a note that admission is free for currently enrolled students. The society is asking the communications desk to review the poster's use of the college wordmark before printing. The wordmark is not yet cleared for this use. The student center allows posters on the north display panel, while the library noticeboard requires approval from its desk staff; volunteers should not assume that permission for one location covers the other. The society would like to post the digital version on September 21, if the wordmark review is complete by then. If the review is still pending on September 21, the coordinator wants to hold the digital post and use a text-only listing in the weekly bulletin instead. The printed copies are to wait until the wordmark question is resolved, even if that means they are not available for the first week of publicity.

The draft budget lists $180 for the three screening licenses, $36 for printing, and $24 for refreshments. The $180 license figure is the total quoted amount, not a per-film amount; it covers the three listed program dates, subject to the distributor's final confirmation of the City in Rain runtime. The printing figure covers 60 standard copies and 18 large-print copies, and the society has asked the campus print desk whether both sizes can be charged to the same order. The refreshments amount is a ceiling for bottled water and packaged snacks, not an instruction to spend the full amount. The treasurer has asked the student activities office whether the society may use its remaining $90 from the fall events allocation toward these costs. That balance is recorded in the society's spreadsheet, but the office has not confirmed that it is available for this program. Until there is a reply, the $90 should remain a possible contribution rather than being subtracted from the total budget request.

The society is also checking whether a short introduction by filmmaker Jo Alvarez is possible for the October 15 program. Alvarez's assistant said, "Jo may be in town that week, but we cannot confirm a visit yet." The coordinator is asking the assistant to confirm availability by September 28. No travel or appearance payment is included in the current budget, and the society has not asked Alvarez to attend remotely. If the assistant confirms a visit, the coordinator wants to ask the events office whether the room can be entered 15 minutes earlier that evening; if there is no confirmation by September 28, the screening should continue with the standard welcome by the program coordinator. The draft should therefore leave Alvarez's name out of the public poster for now, while keeping the possible introduction in the internal schedule notes.

The remaining planning questions are the distributor's confirmed runtime for City in Rain, the operation of the elevator, the room's early-unlock time, the wordmark review, and whether the $90 allocation can be used. Mina Patel is following up with the events office about access and room opening, while the program coordinator is handling the distributor and publicity questions. The treasurer will contact the student activities office about the allocation. The society wants those separate replies recorded against the relevant dates and costs, rather than treating any pending item as settled. The October 8 attendance estimate of 74 should remain in the working file until registration opens, and the door volunteers will use the actual entry count on the evening itself.
